newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine sees IMF standby at $600-800 million.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine sees IMF standby at $600-800 million.

text.p: The head of Ukraine's National Agency for Reconstruction and Development estimated on Thursday the former Soviet republic would receive between $600 and $800 million under an International Monetary Fund stand-by programme.
"It will be between $600 and $800 million," Roman Shpek said at a news conference. "It depends on negotiations and compromises."
An IMF board is due to approve the one-year credit, to be in place until Ukraine meets conditions for a larger, longer-term Extended Fund Facility (EFF) loan, at the end of August.
An unnamed IMF source said in Washington this week the credit would be $550 million.

"The money is not so important, although everyone needs money. Relations with the IMF are more important than the sum of the money," Shpek said, adding the credit would be used to replenish hard currency reserves.
Shpek said Ukraine intended almost immediately to apply to begin negotiations for the three-year, $2.7-2.9 billion EFF.

He also said Ukraine hoped to qualify for four World Bank credits of $250-300 million each which could be used for deficit financing -- credits which could not be delivered until Ukraine agreed a programme with the IMF.
Shpek added Ukraine had met all conditions to qualify for a 130 million ECU ($140 million) deficit financing credit from the European Union.
"After standby talks we will talk with the EU about financial help with balance of payments in 1997," he said. "We will also talk with the Japanese government."
The deficit, contained in the 1997 budget which was passed at the end of June, has been set at 5.7 percent of gross domestic product, or four percent by IMF calculations.
